content: This unique case involved the division of a family tomb built on municipal land,. The court had to distinguish between different types of cemetery rights. The interpretive problem was whether the "ius sepulchri" (right to burial) followed the same rules as the physical structure. The court ruled that while the property rights to the structure are common and divisible (requiring a settlement payment), the right to be buried is a personal, fundamental, and indivisible right that remains attached to the individuals regardless of the property division.
